opening_message:
Ticket 1: Richard Davis (employee ID E011) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E011.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Richard Davis (E011) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Payroll. As a full-time employee whose role owns the Payroll system, write is within policy; recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Richard Davis (E011) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Requested write exceeds max; recommend granting read.
reason: There is conflicting evidence about Richard Davis (E011). HR reports full-time Payroll Specialist (role owns Payroll; write allowed), while Security reports contractor with basic security training (max is read; write requires advanced training). Given the unresolved conflict, I grant the most permissive level that is within policy under both interpretations: read. Granting write would violate policy if the Security record (contractor/basic training) is correct.
